To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human mesothelial cell lines are susceptible to SV40 and BKV infection, and only SV40 causes mesothelial cell transformation.
BKV and SV 40 infected mesothelioma cells, expressed viral oncogenes, altered cell regulatory genes and caused mesothelioma cell transformation and lysis, respectively.
human mesothelial (MM) cells can be infected with polyomaviruses (BK and SV) but not with JC virus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of human papovaviruses and their role in oncogenesis.
the development of novel therapies for mesothelioma.
the molecular mechanisms of mesothelial cell transformation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SV40 is a human mesothelial carcinogen, whereas BKV and JCV are not.
SV40 is the only known polyomavirus that is able to cause malignant transformation.
BKV, like SV40, is capable of infecting mesothelial cells; however, unlike SV40, BKV does not transform human mesothelial cell lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BKV, like SV40, can infect and transform mesothelial cells but does not cause cell lysis and thus is not a candidate for mesothelioma.
SV40 is more efficient at transforming mesothelial cells compared to the other two polyomaviruses.
the human polyomaviruse BKV and JCV are not involved in mesotheliomas, while SV40 may be a risk factor for mesothelioma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the susceptibility of human cells to polyomaviruses is not a function of cell type.
the susceptibility of mesothelial cells for transformation is dependent on the virus strain, and not on the polyomavirus family.
BKV, like SV40, can infect human mesothelium and induce malignant transformation.
